title: AJIN machine learning predicts atomic layer deposition outcomes from experimental precursor-substrate data
summary: AJIN, a graph-neural-network framework trained on 560 experimentally observed ALD and area-selective ALD outcomes (76 precursors, 27 substrates, 20 reactants, 25-620 C), reaches 79.2% balanced accuracy for adsorption and 84.8% for deposition. Tested against the authors' own laboratory ALD experiments, it correctly predicted 83% of new-substrate cases and 71% of new precursor-substrate adsorption cases.
ai_technology: AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Network) with graph-neural-network embeddings (CHGNet-MLP best model)
organization: Incheon National University; Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: Predicted adsorption and deposition outcomes for new substrates and new precursor-substrate pairs were compared with the authors' laboratory ALD experiments.
evidence.unknown: Transfer to unseen precursors is only partial, according to the abstract; per-case details of the laboratory tests are not given in the reviewed material.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning framework predicting whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields ALD, with SHAP and ablation analyses of the drivers.
